source.title: On the Role of Label Noise in the Feature Learning Process
source.authors: Andi Han; Wei Huang; Zhan-Peng Zhou; Gang Niu; Wuyang Chen; Jun-Chi Yan; Akiko Takeda; Taiji Suzuki

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Analyzes and experimentally examines how label noise affects learning, using a different setup from fitting completely random labels.
record.gate_note: The paper studies randomly flipped labels at specified rates, not completely random labels. It does not compare training time against true labels or test shuffled or Gaussian inputs. Figure 1 and Figure 2 results are described in text; precise figure values are not stated.
record.test_reason: The study directly analyzes and measures signal learning followed by noisy-label memorization (V6), and examines training fit and generalization under partial random label corruption (V4), using two-layer CNN theory and synthetic and binary CIFAR-10 experiments.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that signal learning precedes noisy-label memorization, with later memorization degrading generalization under their setup. They also derive theoretical support for early stopping and small-loss sample selection, and report supporting synthetic and CIFAR-10 experiments.
record.recipe_differences: Studies label flipping with a signal-noise data distribution and a two-layer CNN theory, plus synthetic and CIFAR-10 experiments. It does not reproduce the original completely random-label experiment.
record.method_sensitivity: The experiments vary label-noise ratio and, for synthetic data, signal strength; additional figure-only sweeps are shown in Figures 3 and 4.
record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning, Proceedings of Machine Learning Research 267 (2025)
record.problems: The theoretical analysis is limited to a two-layer CNN and random label noise. The authors note it may not capture deeper architectures. Experimental text gives qualitative curve descriptions without exact accuracy values or uncertainty estimates.

untested.parts: Completely random training labels, chance-level test performance, and fitting without changing architecture or training hyperparameters.
A measured small constant-factor training-time comparison and convergence slowing with increasing corruption. Similar theoretical convergence bounds do not establish these comparisons.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or entirely Gaussian-noise inputs. Gaussian noise patches accompanying a class signal do not test this version.

Perfect fitting throughout a corruption sweep from none to fully random labels, and steadily increasing test error reaching chance. Experiments cover flip probabilities 0.1–0.25; the theory assumes nonzero class-specific flip probabilities below one half.
Effects of weight decay, dropout and data augmentation on random-label fitting, and true-label generalization after removing these regularizers.
Learning dynamics under completely random labels and architectures or noise mechanisms beyond those studied. The theory concerns a restricted signal-noise distribution and two-layer CNN.

missing.what: Noisy-sample accuracy initially decreases and subsequently reaches perfect classification at each flip probability 0.1, 0.15, 0.2 and 0.25. These additional conditions are explicitly described in the caption but have no rows.
At flip probability 0.2, VGG test accuracy remains consistently below the otherwise comparable clean-label model. R5 records only the clean model's trajectory, omitting this direct comparison.
missing.locator: Section 6.2, The Two Stage Picture: Accuracy; Figure 2 left

missing.what: Synthetic coefficient trajectories show signal dominance early and noisy-sample noise coefficients overtaking signal later. The clean-label control retains signal dominance and high training accuracy.
missing.locator: Section 6.1; Figure 1 top panels and clean-label bottom panel

missing.what: Additional synthetic trajectories vary flip probability at mu = 20 across 0.1, 0.15, 0.2 and 0.25, and signal strength at probability 0.2 across mu = 15, 20 and 25. Extract readable trajectories without inventing numerical endpoints. The Figure 3 caption's orange-stage description appears inconsistent with its stated stage interpretation.

The clean-label theoretical comparator establishes correct classification of all training samples, arbitrarily small loss and a test-error upper bound that becomes small under the stated signal-strength condition.
missing.locator: Section 4.3, Theorem 4.4; Appendix D.2, Theorem D.6

record.verdict_notes: Missing coverage of full corruption or chance-level error does not justify limits_scope. No recorded result establishes absent or reversed behavior. The theoretical test-error result depends on a deliberately constructed test distribution containing training noise patches; it should not be presented as an unrestricted result for independent fresh inputs. Figure curves were unavailable in the supplied text, so experimental judgments use explicit prose and captions.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test a completely random labeling of the training set or report test error at chance.
Does not compare training time for noisy versus true labels or report how convergence time changes across corruption fractions.
Does not test shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Does not establish a steady test-error rise to chance across noise fractions from none to all; theoretical results assume nonzero label-flipping probabilities below one half.
Does not test weight decay, dropout or data augmentation.
Tests a two-layer CNN theoretically and syntheticly, and VGG nets on two CIFAR-10 categories; does not test the cited Arpit et al. setup.

rows.subject: two-layer CNN
rows.operation_detail: Theoretical analysis of gradient descent with logistic loss on clean and label-flipped samples.
rows.measure: Training loss and classification of clean and noisy training samples at a time when loss is at most ϵ.
rows.value: There exists t* with LS(W(t*)) ≤ ϵ; all clean samples are classified correctly, and a constant fraction of noisy samples are classified according to their noisy labels.
rows.note: The theorem establishes arbitrarily small loss and fitting of a constant fraction of noisy samples, not perfect classification of every training sample.
rows.check: The note incorrectly treats the constant-fraction guarantee as evidence of incomplete fitting. Arbitrarily small average logistic loss implies training error at most epsilon/log(2); for a fixed training set, loss below log(2)/n implies every observed label is classified correctly. This supports the fitting component under Condition 4.1, without establishing a noise-rate trend.

source_check.correct: Under Condition 4.1, for arbitrary epsilon > 0 there exists t* with LS(W(t*)) <= epsilon; all clean samples and a constant fraction of noisy samples satisfy the stated classification guarantees. Arbitrarily small average logistic loss additionally implies arbitrarily small training error.
source_check.locator_found: Condition 4.1; Theorem 4.2, pp. 4–5; logistic-loss definition, Section 3.
source_check.problem: The value is supported, but the note understates the training-fit implication of arbitrarily small logistic loss.

rows.subject: two-layer CNN
rows.operation_detail: Theoretical analysis of test error after training with label flips.
rows.measure: 0-1 test error on the paper's test distribution.
rows.note: A lower bound tied to the flip rates is reported; the theorem does not show test error reaches chance.
rows.check: The lower bound is established under the stated assumptions; failure to prove chance-level error is untested coverage, not a partial effect. Specify that the test distribution reuses uniformly sampled training noise patches with added Gaussian noise. A rate-dependent lower bound does not establish that actual test error increases monotonically.

source_check.correct: L0-1_D(W(t*)) >= 0.5 min{tau+, tau-}, under Condition 4.1. Test inputs contain a uniformly sampled training noise patch plus fresh Gaussian noise; targets remain ground truth.

rows.subject: two-layer CNN
rows.operation_detail: Gradient descent on synthetic data with label-flipping probability 0.1; 200 iterations, learning rate η = 0.1.
rows.measure: Accuracy on noisy training samples over training iterations.
rows.note: Text says noisy-sample accuracy initially drops to 0, then gradually increases; precise curve values are figure-only.
rows.check: Section 6.1 explicitly reports noisy-label accuracy dropping to 0 and subsequently increasing, supporting the temporal ordering. The text does not establish final perfect fitting or test-error degradation for this row, so remove V4. Replace the unspecified value with the reported qualitative trajectory.

source_check.correct: Noisy-training-sample accuracy initially drops to 0 and then gradually increases. The text does not specify its final accuracy. The stated synthetic setup, 200 iterations and learning rate 0.1 are correct.
source_check.problem: The value is not exclusively figure-only: the text explicitly states the drop to 0 and subsequent increase.

rows.subject: VGG net
rows.operation_detail: SGD on the first two CIFAR-10 categories, with each sample's label flipped with probability 0.2.
rows.measure: Accuracy on noisy training samples over epochs.
rows.note: Text reports an initial accuracy drop followed by a gradual increase to 1; precise curve values are figure-only.
rows.check: Section 6.2 explicitly reports an initial decrease followed by noisy-label accuracy reaching 1. Record that endpoint instead of 'figure only'. This demonstrates noisy-subset fitting and temporal ordering at flip probability 0.2; it does not alone establish perfect accuracy on the entire training set.

source_check.correct: At flip probability 0.2, noisy-training-sample accuracy initially drops and then gradually increases to 1; test accuracy remains below the clean-label comparator.
source_check.locator_found: Section 6.2, The Two Stage Picture: Accuracy, p. 8; Figure 2, left.
source_check.problem: The endpoint 1 and temporal trajectory are explicitly stated in the text, rather than being figure-only.

rows.subject: VGG net
rows.operation_detail: SGD on the first two CIFAR-10 categories, under nearly identical settings without label flipping.
rows.measure: Training and test accuracy over epochs.
rows.note: Text says training and test accuracies consistently increase; exact values are figure-only.
rows.check: Retain as the clean-label comparator. The text reports increasing training and test accuracy but gives no endpoint establishing perfect training fit. The comparison with lower test accuracy under label noise is missing from the extracted values.

rows.subject: two-layer CNN
rows.operation_detail: Theoretical analysis of the first stage under label flipping.
rows.measure: Classification of clean and noisy training samples at T1.
rows.value: All clean samples are classified correctly; all noisy samples are classified according to their ground-truth classes.
rows.note: The result states that early learning fits clean samples while ignoring noisy labels.
rows.check: Correct under Condition 4.1. Include the signal-strength, overparameterization, small-initialization and learning-rate assumptions rather than presenting the flip-rate restriction as the complete condition.

source_check.correct: At T1, clean samples are correctly classified and flipped samples are classified according to their ground-truth classes. The guarantee requires all of Condition 4.1, beyond the listed flip-rate restriction.
source_check.locator_found: Theorem 4.1 and its explanatory paragraph; Condition 4.1, p. 4.

rows.subject: two-layer CNN
rows.operation_detail: Theoretical analysis of later training with label flipping.
rows.measure: Training loss, clean-sample classification, and noisy-sample classification.
rows.baseline: Stage I behavior described in Theorem 4.1.
rows.value: At loss ≤ ϵ, all clean samples remain correctly classified and a constant fraction of noisy samples are classified according to their noisy labels.
rows.note: The result describes a later shift toward fitting noisy labels.
rows.check: Correct as a later-stage memorization result paired with R6. It overlaps R1 and should not be counted as independent evidence.

rows.subject: VGG net
rows.operation_detail: SGD on the first two CIFAR-10 categories with label flipping; SHAP visualizations at selected epochs.
rows.measure: SHAP visualizations of predictions on noisy samples.
rows.note: Text describes recognizable features at epochs 1 and 41, and messy interpretations with background noise at epochs 81 and 121.
rows.check: Record the textual interpretation: recognizable class features at epochs 1 and 41, followed by messy background-related attributions at epochs 81 and 121. These are indirect qualitative evidence about feature use; SHAP alone does not establish memorization or its magnitude.

source_check.correct: Text describes recognizable class features at epochs 1 and 41, followed by messy interpretations involving background noise at epochs 81 and 121. State: cannot_determine for V6 from this measure alone; retain as qualitative corroboration.
source_check.locator_found: Section 6.2, Visualization of the Feature Learning Process, pp. 8–9; Figure 2, right.
source_check.problem: The interpretation is stated in text; indirect SHAP evidence does not establish an incomplete V6 effect, so partial is inappropriate.
